mainTopic: Why the משנה names מנחת חוטא, and רב's ruling that a קומץ taken by a זר is put back, following בן בתירא
overview: The amud opens by finishing the question of why the משנה names מנחת חוטא separately. The answer is that even according to רבי שמעון, who keeps a sinner's offering plain, an unfit person's קמיצה makes it פסול, and this משנה follows his view. Next, רב rules that if a זר took the קומץ, it is put back into the מנחה. After failed attempts to fit this with the רבנן of the משנה, the גמרא says רב follows בן בתירא. It then tests what new point רב adds, discussing the left hand on יום הכפורים, a זר doing שחיטה, the פרה אדומה, נגעים, and a בָּמָה. A ברייתא shows that בן בתירא was already lenient for every disqualification. So the גמרא says רב's real point is that the קומץ goes back even after it was sanctified in a כלי שרת. A second version says the opposite: it goes back only before it was sanctified. רב נחמן questions the logic of the תנאים who make the כלי the cutoff, and then explains it himself. A new challenge to his explanation begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's view could make us think the sinner's מנחה stays valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי שמעון, who says a sinner's offering is kept plain, and explains why the משנה had to name מנחת חוטא separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבי שמעון says a sinner's offering should really have extras] so that the sinner should not profit. Then why does it not need them? So that his offering should not look fancy. You might have thought: since רבי שמעון says the sinner's offering should not be fancy, then even if unfit people take its handful it should be valid. So the משנה teaches us that it is still פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends a quote from רבי שמעון about why a sinner's offering is kept plain. It uses that idea to explain why the משנה mentions מנחת חוטא by name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that a sinner's offering is purposely made less 'beautiful'. From that, one might reason that a low-quality קמיצה by an unfit person would not ruin it, since it is not supposed to be fancy anyway. The משנה names מנחת חוטא to block that idea: it is still פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Gaining, profiting
Requires (here: requires extra items like נסכים)
Beautified, of high quality
You might have thought to say
People unfit for the Temple service
So it teaches us (the new point)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי שמעון as saying the sinner's offering doesn't matter. He only says it is kept plain; it still needs a proper, valid עבודה.

phrases.english: so that the sinner will not profit.
And for what reason does it not require [them]?
So that his offering will not be of superior quality.
It might enter your mind to say:
Since Rabbi Shimon says
that his offering should not be of superior quality,
when unfit people remove its handful,
it should also be valid,
so [the משנה] teaches us [that it is not].

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא הוֹאִיל וְאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun just before this section to the question of why מנחת חוטא is named separately in the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the extra wording as blocking a mistaken inference from רבי שמעון's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי שמעון keeps the sinner's offering plain, a קמיצה by an unfit person should be acceptable for it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even according to רבי שמעון, a מנחת חוטא whose handful was taken by an unfit person is פסול.

steps.title: Then the parallel משנה about animal offerings should name חטאת חלב too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if that reasoning is right, the משנה in זבחים should also name חטאת חלב separately, but it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, there too [in זבחים] the משנה should teach: 'Both the חטאת for eating forbidden fat and all the animal offerings whose blood was received by a non-כהן or an אונן are פסול,' and we would say it was needed for רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the previous answer by pointing to a similar משנה about animal offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's 'keep it plain' idea also applies to חטאת חלב, which doesn't get נסכים. So by the same logic the זבחים משנה should have named חטאת חלב separately. Since it didn't, the logic of the previous answer looks weak.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge from the previous answer)
The חטאת brought for accidentally eating forbidden fat
A non-כהן
A mourner on the day a close relative died, who may not serve
It was necessary

phrases.english: If so,
there as well let it teach:
phrases.notes: 'There' means the משנה in זבחים about animal offerings.

phrases.english: Both the sin offering of forbidden fat
and all the slaughtered offerings
whose blood a non-priest or an acute mourner collected,
and let us say: it was necessary for Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי הָתָם נָמֵי לִיתְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 1 by applying its logic to a parallel משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה names מנחת חוטא separately because of רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same logic would require the זבחים משנה to name חטאת חלב, yet it does not.

steps.title: The word 'all' already includes everything
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge: the word 'all' with no 'except' already covers every case, so naming מנחת חוטא seems unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: It seems that since [the זבחים משנה] says 'all' and does not say 'except', everything is included. Here too, since [our משנה] says 'all' and does not say 'except', everything is included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its question by explaining what the זבחים משנה shows us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a משנה says 'all' and lists no exceptions, every case is included, even חטאת חלב for רבי שמעון. Our משנה also says 'all' with no 'except', so מנחת חוטא is already included. So why name it?

keyTerms.meaning: It seems, apparently (drawing a conclusion)
All
Except
Implied, included in the meaning

phrases.english: Apparently, since he taught "all"
and does not teach "except",
all of them are implied.
Here too, since he taught "all"
and does not teach "except", all of them are implied.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא כֵּיוָן דִּתְנָא לֵיהּ כֹּל וְלָא קָתָנֵי חוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of step 2 by drawing out its implication for our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to name מנחת חוטא separately
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'All' with no 'except' already includes מנחת חוטא, as shown by the זבחים משנה.

steps.title: Naming it shows this משנה can follow רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that naming מנחת חוטא was needed, because the earlier משנה was explained as not following רבי שמעון, and we might think this one doesn't either.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: since we explained the earlier משנה as not following רבי שמעון, the later משנה also does not follow רבי שמעון. So it teaches us [that it does].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reason why our משנה, unlike the זבחים one, had to name מנחת חוטא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה in this perek was explained as not following רבי שמעון. Without naming מנחת חוטא, we would assume this משנה also doesn't follow him. Naming it shows that this משנה fits רבי שמעון's view too; the זבחים משנה had no such issue.

keyTerms.meaning: We established, we explained (a source as following a certain view)
The first part (here: the earlier משנה)
The later part (here: our משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה names מנחת חוטא to show that, even for רבי שמעון, a sinner's מנחה is פסול when an unfit person takes its handful, and that this משנה follows his view even though the earlier one did not.

phrases.english: It was necessary,
since it might enter your mind to say:
since we established the first clause
phrases.notes: The 'first clause' is the first משנה of this perek, which the גמרא earlier explained as not following רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: as not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon,
the last clause too is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon,
so it teaches us [otherwise].

steps.triggerLanguage: אִצְטְרִיךְ סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא הוֹאִיל וְאוֹקֵימְנָא לְרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 2-3 by showing why our משנה differs from the זבחים משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: our משנה had a special reason to name it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the earlier משנה does not follow רבי שמעון, this one doesn't either.
steps.terutzMaskana: Naming מנחת חוטא shows this משנה is in line with רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רב: a non-priest's handful is put back
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that if a זר took the קומץ from a מנחה, the קומץ is put back into the מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: If a non-כהן took the handful, he should put it back.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב gives a ruling about a קומץ that was taken by a זר, someone who is not a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking the קומץ is a job for a כהן, so a זר doing it is a problem. רב says the fix is to put the קומץ back into the מנחה, so a fit כהן can take it again. This ruling will now be tested against the wording of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who is not a כהן
Who took the קומץ (the handful of flour) out of a מנחה
He should put it back

phrases.english: Rav said:
A non-priest who took the handful should put it back,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: זָר שֶׁקָּמַץ – יַחְזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion, separate from the topic of מנחת חוטא in steps 1-4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קומץ taken by a זר is returned to the מנחה, and the מנחה can still be used.

steps.title: But the משנה says he disqualified it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the משנה says a זר who takes the קומץ פסל the מנחה. That sounds final, not fixable.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה that he 'disqualified' it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב using the word פסל in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה says the זר disqualified the מנחה, the plain meaning is that the מנחה is ruined. Then putting the קומץ back should not help, which goes against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, here is a source against you
He disqualified it, made it unfit
We

phrases.english: But we learned 'he disqualified'?
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה that lists people, a זר among them, whose taking of the קומץ makes the מנחה unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אֲנַן ״פָּסַל״ תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the קומץ is returned (step 5).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's word 'disqualified' implies the מנחה is permanently unfit, which contradicts returning the קומץ.

steps.title: Disqualified only until he puts it back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'disqualified' means the מנחה is unfit only until the קומץ is returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'disqualified' mean? It is disqualified until he puts it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by reading the משנה's word in a narrower way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is temporary. As long as the קומץ is sitting in the זר's hand, the מנחה can't go forward. Once it is put back, a fit כהן can take the קומץ again.

keyTerms.meaning: What is meant by?
Until he puts it back
The act of taking the handful from a מנחה

phrases.english: What does 'disqualified' mean?
It is disqualified until he puts it back.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״פָּסַל״? פָּסַל עַד שֶׁיַּחֲזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Disqualified' means unfit only until the קומץ is returned.

steps.title: Then רב is just בן בתירא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this reading makes the first opinion in the משנה the same as בן בתירא's.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, that is exactly בן בתירא's opinion?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בן בתירא says a קומץ taken the wrong way, with the left hand, is put back and taken again. If the רבנן also hold that the קומץ is put back, then the two opinions say the same thing. So why does the משנה present them as a disagreement?

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if what you said is true
That is the same as

phrases.english: If so, that is the same as Ben Beteira?
phrases.notes: בן בתירא, in that same משנה, says a קומץ taken with the left hand is put back and taken again with the right.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הַיְינוּ בֶּן בְּתִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading 'disqualified until he returns it' (step 7).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading removes any difference between the רבנן and בן בתירא, who argue in the משנה.

steps.title: They argue only when the handful is missing some
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if the קומץ is still whole, everyone agrees it is put back. The argument is about a קומץ that lost some flour: may he refill it from his own flour at home?
steps.simpleTranslation: If the קומץ is still complete, the רבנן do not disagree with בן בתירא. They disagree when the קומץ is missing some. The רבנן hold he may not bring flour from his house to fill it up, and בן בתירא holds he may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps רב's reading by finding a different point the two opinions argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the קומץ is whole, both sides say to put it back, so רב's ruling fits everyone. The real argument is about a קומץ that lost some flour. The רבנן say you can't top it up with flour from home, so that מנחה stays unfit. בן בתירא says you can top it up.

keyTerms.meaning: In its original state, still whole
They argue
The handful is missing some flour
From his own house, his own flour
And fill it up

phrases.english: If the handful is still in its original state –

phrases.aramaic: לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּבֶן בְּתִירָא,
phrases.english: the Rabbis do not disagree with Ben Beteira,
where they disagree is when the handful is missing some.
The Rabbis hold:
He may not bring flour from his house and fill it up,
Ben Beteira holds:
He may bring flour from his house and fill it up.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דְּאִיתֵיהּ לְקוֹמֶץ בְּעֵינֵיהּ – לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּבֶן בְּתִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by moving the argument to a different case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן and בן בתירא argue about whether a whole קומץ can be returned.
steps.terutzMaskana: They agree a whole קומץ is returned. They argue only about refilling a קומץ that is missing some flour.

steps.title: Then the משנה should mention refilling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that if the argument were about refilling, בן בתירא's words in the משנה should mention bringing flour from home, and they don't.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, how can the משנה say 'בן בתירא says: he puts it back and takes the handful again with his right hand'? It should have said 'he puts it back, brings flour from his house and fills it up, and takes the handful again with his right hand'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 9 from the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If refilling were the whole point of the argument, the משנה would surely say so in בן בתירא's opinion. Since his words only say 'put it back and take again', the משנה seems to be talking about a whole קומץ. That brings back the problem of step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: It should have said
And do it again
With the right hand

phrases.english: If so, Ben Beteira says:
'He puts it back and again takes the handful with the right hand'?!
'Ben Beteira says: He puts it back
and brings flour from his house and fills it up,
and again takes the handful with the right hand,'
is what it should have said!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, בֶּן בְּתִירָא אוֹמֵר: יַחְזִיר וְיַחֲזוֹר וְיִקְמוֹץ בְּיָמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the argument is about refilling a קומץ that is missing some (step 9).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בן בתירא's wording in the משנה does not mention refilling, so the argument can't be about refilling.

steps.title: רב was following בן בתירא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives up on fitting רב with the רבנן and says that רב's ruling follows בן בתירא's opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב said this, he said it according to בן בתירא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes a new approach. 'Disqualified' keeps its plain meaning for the רבנן, and רב is following the other opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there's no need to stretch the word 'disqualified'. The רבנן hold the מנחה is really unfit, and רב's ruling of putting the קומץ back follows בן בתירא. This sets up the next question: why would רב need to say that?

keyTerms.meaning: When he said it
Here: according to the opinion of

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָא אָמַר רַב לְבֶן בְּתִירָא,
phrases.english: When Rav said it, he said it according to Ben Beteira,

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָא אָמַר רַב לְבֶן בְּתִירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 10 knocks down the earlier answers, this offers a new explanation of רב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the ruling to one side of the argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's ruling fits the רבנן, the first opinion in the משנה.

steps.title: But that is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב needed to say it if he is only repeating בן בתירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer: if רב only repeats בן בתירא's view, what does he add?
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן בתירא already said in the משנה that the קומץ is put back. A ruling that only repeats an opinion in the משנה seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why say it?

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב follows בן בתירא (step 11).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רב only repeats בן בתירא, his statement adds nothing.

steps.title: בן בתירא's rule covers all the unfit people
steps.stepSummary: רב's point is new. We might have thought בן בתירא allows putting the קומץ back only when it was taken with the left hand. רב teaches that it also works for a זר and the other unfit people.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that בן בתירא allows it only when the left hand was used, but not for the other disqualifications. So רב teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' question by showing what new thing רב adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בן בתירא speaks only about a קומץ taken with the left hand. רב adds that the same fix works for a זר and the other unfit people listed in the משנה. So רב's ruling makes בן בתירא's opinion wider.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said
He rules it fit
With the left hand
The other people or problems that make it unfit
So he teaches us otherwise

steps.whatToRemember: For now, the גמרא says רב follows בן בתירא and extends his rule beyond the left hand to a זר and the other unfit people. Later (steps 23-26) the גמרא shows this was already known from a ברייתא, and it gives רב a different new point.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב is siding with the רבנן. The earlier tries to fit him with the רבנן were rejected. In the end he follows בן בתירא and widens his rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a ruling that seems to just repeat a משנה can actually teach something new, by stretching one opinion to cover more cases.

phrases.english: You might have said:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא מַכְשַׁר בֶּן בְּתִירָא אֶלָּא בִּשְׂמֹאל,
phrases.english: Ben Beteira rules it fit only with the left hand,
but not with the other disqualifications,
so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא מַכְשַׁר בֶּן בְּתִירָא אֶלָּא בִּשְׂמֹאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows what new thing the ruling teaches
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בן בתירא allows putting the קומץ back only when the left hand was used.
steps.terutzMaskana: בן בתירא allows it for all the disqualifications in the משנה, including a זר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For now, רב's ruling is read as extending בן בתירא's rule to every unfit person. Step 26 later replaces this with a different new point.

steps.title: Why would the left hand be more special than a non-priest?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we would have limited בן בתירא to the left hand. The left hand is valid on יום הכפורים, but a זר is also valid in one place: שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is so special about the left hand, because we find it is valid on יום הכפורים? We also find that a non-priest is valid, for slaughtering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the חידוש from step 13. Why would anyone think the left hand gets better treatment than a זר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe the left hand seems less bad because on יום הכפורים the כהן גדול uses his left hand for a real service. But a זר is also allowed to do something: he may slaughter a קרבן. So both have a case where they are valid, and רב's teaching seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why treat this case differently?
A case where it is valid
A non-כהן
Slaughtering the animal

phrases.english: What is different about the left hand
that we find it valid on יום הכפורים?
phrases.notes: On יום כפור the כהן גדול carries the pan of incense into the Holy of Holies in his left hand.

phrases.english: A non-priest too, we find him
valid for slaughtering!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא שְׂמֹאל דְּאַשְׁכְּחַן לֵהּ הֶכְשֵׁירָא בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the hava amina given in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 13 that we would have limited בן בתירא to the left hand
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both the left hand and a זר have a case where they are valid, so there is no reason to treat the left hand better.

steps.title: Slaughtering is not a real Temple service
steps.stepSummary: שחיטה is not counted as an עבודה, so a זר is never valid for a real service.
steps.simpleTranslation: Slaughtering is not a Temple service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a זר being allowed to slaughter does not count, because slaughtering is not a real עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The left hand is valid for a true עבודה on יום הכפורים. A זר is never valid for a true עבודה, since שחיטה does not qualify. So it made sense to think the left hand is better, and רב had to teach that a זר is included too.

keyTerms.meaning: A Temple service that must be done by a כהן
Not

phrases.english: Slaughtering is not a Temple service.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁחִיטָה לָאו עֲבוֹדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the case brought against us is not a true עבודה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A זר is valid for שחיטה just as the left hand is valid on יום הכפורים
steps.terutzMaskana: שחיטה is not an עבודה, so a זר is never valid for a real service, unlike the left hand

steps.title: But a non-priest may not slaughter the red heifer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that שחיטה is not an עבודה. רב himself said a פרה אדומה slaughtered by a זר is invalid, because the Torah says אלעזר and חוקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really not a service? But רבי זירא said in the name of רב: if a non-priest slaughters the פרה אדומה, it is invalid. And רב said about it: "אלעזר" and "חוקה" are written about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 15. It brings a case where slaughtering does need a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the slaughter of the פרה אדומה must be done by a כהן, that looks like proof that שחיטה is a real עבודה. The proof comes from the פסוקים that name אלעזר the כהן and call it a חוקה, meaning every detail must be followed.

keyTerms.meaning: The red heifer (פרה אדומה)
Invalid
Statute; the details must be done exactly as written

phrases.english: And is it not?
But didn't רבי זירא say in the name of רב:
slaughtering the heifer by a non-priest is invalid
And רב said about it:
"Elazar" and "statute" are written about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שחיטה is not an עבודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The slaughter of the פרה must be done by a כהן, which suggests that שחיטה is an עבודה.

steps.title: The red heifer is a different kind of holy item
steps.stepSummary: פרה אדומה is different, because it counts as קדשי בדק הבית and not as a קרבן for the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: The red heifer is different, because it is sanctified for Temple upkeep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we cannot learn about normal קרבנות from the פרה, because the פרה belongs to a different category.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרה is not brought on the מזבח. It counts as holy property of the Temple treasury. So its special rule, that a כהן must slaughter it, tells us nothing about שחיטה of real קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
Items made holy for the upkeep of the בית המקדש, not for the מזבח

phrases.english: The heifer is different,
because it is sanctified for Temple upkeep.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי פָּרָה דְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between categories of holy items
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פרה shows that שחיטה is an עבודה
steps.terutzMaskana: פרה is קדשי בדק הבית, so its rule does not apply to קרבנות

steps.title: Shouldn't altar offerings need a כהן even more?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back with a קל וחומר. If בדק הבית items need a כהן, then altar items, which are holier, should surely need one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it all the more so? Items sanctified for Temple upkeep need a כהן, and items sanctified for the altar don't need a כהן?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the distinction of step 17 using a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדשי מזבח are holier than קדשי בדק הבית. If even the less holy פרה must be slaughtered by a כהן, then all the more so a קרבן should need a כהן for שחיטה. That would make שחיטה an עבודה again.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so; this is a קל וחומר
Being a כהן; priesthood
Items made holy to be offered on the מזבח

phrases.english: But isn't it all the more so?
Items sanctified for Temple upkeep require a כהן,
and items sanctified for the altar don't require a כהן?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו כָּל דְּכֵן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction in step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the פרה is different because it is קדשי בדק הבית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: what applies to less holy items should surely apply to more holy items.

steps.title: Needing a כהן does not make something a Temple service
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי answers that a task can need a כהן without being an עבודה, just like looking at נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא son of רב אידי said: It is just like examining the shades of נגעים, which are not a Temple service and still need a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא answers the קשיא by showing that needing a כהן and being an עבודה are two separate things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Examining נגעים must be done by a כהן, yet nobody calls it a Temple service. In the same way, the פרה needs a כהן because of its own פסוקים, not because its שחיטה is an עבודה. So the קל וחומר proves nothing, and the answer of step 15 stands: שחיטה is not an עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just like
The shades of צרעת marks, which a כהן must examine

steps.whatToRemember: A task needing a כהן does not make it an עבודה. So שחיטה stays outside the category of עבודה, and the difference between the left hand and a זר stands for now.
steps.confusionAlert: רב שישא is not saying the פרה does not need a כהן. It does. He is only saying that this requirement does not prove its שחיטה is a Temple service.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: רב שישא son of רב אידי said:
It is just like the shades of נגעים,
which are not a Temple service
and yet they require a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַמַּרְאוֹת נְגָעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to a parallel case: needing a כהן is separate from being an עבודה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פרה needs a כהן, its שחיטה must be an עבודה, and קרבנות should be the same
steps.terutzMaskana: Like נגעים, something can need a כהן without being an עבודה, so שחיטה is still not an עבודה

steps.title: Why not learn it from a private altar?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב had to teach his rule about a זר, since we could learn it from a בָּמָה, where a זר was once allowed to serve.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn it from a private altar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for רב's teaching. It suggests the same rule could be learned from a בָּמָה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the בית המקדש was built, even a זר could offer on a private altar. So a זר doing the service was once valid. If so, we could say that a קמיצה done by a זר is not fully ruined and can be redone, without needing רב to tell us.

keyTerms.meaning: A private altar, which was allowed at certain times before the בית המקדש was built
Let us learn (one law from another)

phrases.english: Let us learn it from a private altar!
phrases.notes: On a בָּמָה even a non-כהן could bring offerings, so a זר doing the service was once acceptable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֵילַף מִבָּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing why רב's ruling about a זר makes sense, the גמרא asks why it needed to be taught at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רב's teaching that בן בתירא lets a זר's קמיצה be redone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A זר was valid on a בָּמָה, so the rule could be learned from there, and רב's statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Proof that we do learn from a private altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible answer by bringing a ברייתא that does learn a Temple law from a בָּמָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say we do not learn from a private altar, isn't it taught: From where do we know that something that went out of the courtyard, if it went up on the altar, does not come down? Because something that went out is valid on a private altar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא expects someone to answer, "We don't learn from a בָּמָה." It shoots that answer down with a ברייתא that does learn from a בָּמָה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא deals with a קרבן that left the עזרה and became פסול. It rules that if it already went up on the מזבח, it is not taken down. The reason it gives is that leaving does not disqualify on a בָּמָה. So we see that a Temple law is learned from a בָּמָה, which supports the challenge in step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: Something (like part of a קרבן) that went out of its allowed area, the עזרה
If it went up on the מזבח, it does not come down
Valid

phrases.english: And if you would say: we do not learn from a private altar,
but isn't it taught: From where do we know regarding something that went out,
phrases.notes: This means something that left the Temple courtyard, which makes it unfit.

phrases.english: that if it went up on the altar, it does not come down?
Because something that went out is valid on a private altar!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵימָא, מִבָּמָה לָא יָלְפִינַן, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of step 20 by blocking the answer that we never learn from a בָּמָה.
steps.raayaObject: That Temple laws can be learned from a בָּמָה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says a יוֹצֵא that went up on the מזבח does not come down, because a יוֹצֵא is valid on a בָּמָה

steps.title: The ברייתא really relies on a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's real source is the פסוק "זאת תורת העולה", not the בָּמָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא relies on the verse "This is the law of the burnt offering."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from the ברייתא. The real source of that law is a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that something on the מזבח does not come down is learned from "זאת תורת העולה". The mention of a בָּמָה in the ברייתא is only extra support, not the real source. So the ברייתא does not prove that we learn Temple laws from a בָּמָה, and the challenge of step 20 falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: He relies on it (this is his real source)
"This is the law of the burnt offering", the פסוק used to teach that what goes up on the מזבח stays there

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא was wrong to mention a בָּמָה. The גמרא only says the בָּמָה is not the real source; the פסוק is.

phrases.english: The tanna, on "This is the law of the burnt offering"
relies.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא אַ״זֹּאת תּוֹרַת הָעֹלָה״ סְמִיךְ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא that we learn from a בָּמָה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's real source is a פסוק; the בָּמָה is only a side support
steps.whatToRemember: We do not learn Temple laws from a בָּמָה. The ברייתא about a יוֹצֵא is really based on the פסוק "זאת תורת העולה".

steps.title: בן בתירא already allows all disqualifications
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב was needed, since a ברייתא already says בן בתירא is lenient about every disqualification.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is the reason we know it only because רב taught us? Otherwise I would have said בן בתירא disqualifies in other cases? But isn't it taught: רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה and רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון say: בן בתירא would declare valid in all the disqualifications!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about רב's teaching. A ברייתא already tells us בן בתירא is lenient in every case, so what did רב add?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בן בתירא only spoke about a קמיצה done with the left hand. רב's teaching extended this to a זר. But this ברייתא says בן בתירא allows redoing the קמיצה for all the disqualifications. That already covers a זר, so רב's teaching seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: The other disqualifications (besides using the left hand)
Disqualified, made the offering invalid
Declares valid (here: allows the קמיצה to be redone)

phrases.english: Rather, is the reason because רב taught us,
so that if not for this, I would have said
that with other disqualifications, בן בתירא disqualifies?
But isn't it taught: רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה
and רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון say:
בן בתירא would declare valid
in all of the disqualifications!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא טַעְמָא דְּאַשְׁמְעִינַן רַב, הָא לָאו הָכִי הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the בָּמָה idea is rejected, the גמרא challenges the need for רב's teaching from a different direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רב's teaching that בן בתירא allows a זר's קמיצה to be redone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says בן בתירא is lenient in all disqualifications, which already includes a זר, so רב adds nothing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that בן בתירא's leniency is not limited to the left-hand case. It forces the גמרא to find what new point רב was really teaching.

steps.title: The ברייתא of בן בתירא about a left-handed קמיצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא behind the question. The תנא קמא reads "וקמץ משם" as being about where the קמיצה may be done. בן בתירא reads it as teaching that a handful taken with the left hand is put back and taken again with the right.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: "And he shall remove from there" means from any place where a non-כהן may stand. בן בתירא says: How do we know that if he removed the handful with his left hand, he must put it back and remove it again with his right? The פסוק says "and he shall remove from there," meaning from the place he already removed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא ("ותניא"), which shows the פסוק that בן בתירא learns his rule from. This prepares the next step, which argues that this general source already covers a זר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן בתירא learns from the word "משם" that a handful taken the wrong way is not ruined. It goes back into the מנחה and is taken again properly. This is the source for being lenient about mistakes in קמיצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Removing a fistful of flour from a מנחה to burn on the מזבח
A non-כהן
The left hand, which is not valid for עבודה
He must put it back into the מנחה
The פסוק teaches us

phrases.english: And it is taught: "And he shall remove a handful from there"
from the place where the feet of a non-priest stand.
phrases.notes: He means the קמיצה can be done anywhere in the courtyard, even where a non-כהן is allowed to stand.

phrases.english: Ben Beteira says:
From where do we know that if he removed the handful with the left hand,
he must put it back and again remove the handful with the right?
The verse says: "And he shall remove a handful from there,"
from the place where he already removed the handful.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: ״וְקָמַץ מִשָּׁם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ברייתא to the challenge of step 23. It shows that בן בתירא's source, "וקמץ משם", is a general פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge that רב's ruling is not needed
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: בן בתירא's reading of "וקמץ משם"

steps.title: The פסוק has no limits, so every disqualification should be included
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the question. The פסוק does not say which mistakes it covers, so the left hand should be no different from any other disqualification, including a זר. Then רב's ruling seems unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the פסוק is written without any limits, what difference does it make whether it was the left hand or any other disqualification?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its question on רב. בן בתירא's source already covers a זר, so what did רב add?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only mentions the left hand, but its source, "משם," is general. So the same rule should apply to every invalid קמיצה, including one done by a זר. That makes רב's ruling look like it teaches nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: Written without limits or details
What difference does it make to me?
Things that make an עבודה invalid

phrases.english: And since the verse is written without limits about it,
what difference is it to me whether it was the left hand,
and what difference is it to me whether it was the other disqualifications?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן דִּקְרָא סְתָמָא כְּתִיב בַּהּ, מָה לִי שְׂמֹאל, וּמָה לִי שְׁאָר הַפְּסוּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא just quoted to complete the question against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling about a זר who did קמיצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בן בתירא's general פסוק already covers every disqualification, so רב's ruling is not needed.

steps.title: רב's new point: even after it was sanctified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב adds something new. Even if the invalid handful was already put into a כלי שרת and became sanctified, it can still be returned. This rejects the view of certain תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what רב teaches us: even if he removed the handful and also sanctified it, it is returned. This comes to reject the view of these תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining what רב adds. It also sets up a ברייתא with the opposing view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without רב, we might think a handful can be put back only before it enters a כלי שרת. רב tells us it goes back even after that, so his ruling is not extra.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the new thing he teaches us
He sanctified it by putting it into a כלי שרת
To reject or exclude another opinion
Sages of the משנה era

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not arguing with בן בתירא. He is explaining how far בן בתירא's leniency goes.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן רַב:
phrases.english: Rather, this is what Rav teaches us:
if he removed the handful, and even sanctified it, it is returned,
phrases.notes: "It is returned" is not said here but assumed. To sanctify it means putting the handful into a כלי שרת.

phrases.english: and this comes to exclude the view of these tanna'im,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of steps 23 and 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives רב's ruling a new detail that the ברייתא did not teach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's ruling seems to repeat what בן בתירא's general פסוק already teaches.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב teaches that the handful is returned even after it was sanctified in a כלי שרת.

steps.title: The תנאים who say sanctifying makes it invalid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא of רבי יוסי בן יוסי בן יאסיין and רבי יהודה הנחתום. They say בן בתירא lets the handful be returned only if it was not yet sanctified. Once sanctified, it is invalid, and רב disagrees with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי יוסי בן יוסי בן יאסיין and רבי יהודה הנחתום said: When does this apply? When he removed the handful and did not sanctify it. But if he sanctified it, he made it invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the opinion רב comes to reject. This finishes the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These תנאים put a limit on בן בתירא: putting the invalid handful into a כלי שרת locks in its invalid status. רב says there is no such limit, and that is why his ruling was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case was this said? (a phrase that limits a rule)
He made it invalid
A sacred vessel used in the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, בן בתירא lets an invalid handful be returned even after it was sanctified. רבי יוסי בן יוסי בן יאסיין and רבי יהודה הנחתום say it can be returned only before it was sanctified.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹסֵי בֶּן יָאסְיָין
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yosei ben Yosei ben Yasiyyan
and Rabbi Yehuda the baker said:
In what case is this statement said?
phrases.notes: "This statement" is בן בתירא's ruling that the handful is put back.

phrases.english: Where he removed the handful and did not sanctify it,
but if he sanctified it, he has disqualified it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹסֵי בֶּן יָאסְיָין וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנַּחְתּוֹם אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the opinion that step 26 says רב rejects.
steps.raayaObject: That some תנאים limit בן בתירא's leniency to a handful that was not sanctified
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יוסי בן יוסי בן יאסיין and רבי יהודה הנחתום

steps.title: A second version of רב's ruling
steps.stepSummary: Some say רב allowed returning the handful only before it was sanctified in a כלי, following the תנאים of the ברייתא and not the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: if he only took the handful, yes, it can be returned. If he already sanctified it, no. Whose view is this? It follows those תנאים, and it rejects the view of the תנא קמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of what רב said. In this version, רב allows putting the handful back only if it was not yet placed in a כלי שרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 26, רב's new point was that even a sanctified handful can be returned. In this version רב says the opposite: a sanctified handful cannot be returned. So here רב agrees with רבי יוסי בן יוסי בן יאסיין and רבי יהודה הנחתום and rejects the תנא קמא of their ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: He took the handful (the קמיצה) from the מנחה.
He sanctified it by putting the handful into a כלי שרת.
To exclude, meaning to reject a certain opinion.

steps.confusionAlert: The two versions of רב disagree. Version one (step 26): even after a כלי, it can be returned. Version two (here): only before a כלי.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
If he took the handful, yes,
phrases.notes: Yes, it can be put back and taken again properly.

phrases.english: if he sanctified it, no.
In accordance with whom? In accordance with these תנאים,
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי בן יוסי בן יאסיין and רבי יהודה הנחתום from step 27.

phrases.english: and to exclude the first תנא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רב's answer from step 26, now siding with the תנאים quoted in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative version of the answer: רב's ruling is needed to rule like specific תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's ruling seemed unnecessary because the ברייתא already says בן בתירא allows returning the handful.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב comes to rule like רבי יוסי בן יוסי בן יאסיין and רבי יהודה הנחתום: it can be returned only before it is sanctified.

steps.title: רב נחמן questions the logic of those תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks: either קמיצה by an unfit person counts as a service or it does not. Either way, putting it in a כלי should not change anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן objected: What do these תנאים hold? If an unfit person's קמיצה is a service, it should be invalid even without putting it in a כלי! If it is not a service, then when he put it in a כלי, what happened?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks the view of the תנאים who make the difference depend on whether the handful went into a כלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He sets up two options. If the unfit person's קמיצה is a real service, the מנחה is already ruined at the moment of the קמיצה. If it is not a real service, then putting it in a כלי is also meaningless and should not ruin anything. Either way, the כלי should not be the dividing line.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it, raising a strong objection.
Taking the handful by people who are unfit for Temple service.
A Temple service, an act that counts as part of offering the קרבן.
Putting the handful into a כלי שרת.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman objected to this:
What do these תנאים hold?
If the taking of a handful by unfit people is a service,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא עָבֵיד לֵיהּ מַתַּן כְּלִי!
phrases.english: then even though he did not put it into a vessel, it should be invalid!

phrases.aramaic: אִי קְמִיצַת פְּסוּלִין לָאו עֲבוֹדָה הִיא,
phrases.english: If the taking of a handful by unfit people is not a service,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי עֲבַד לֵהּ מַתַּן כְּלִי מַאי הֲוָה?
phrases.english: then when he put it into a vessel, what happened?
phrases.notes: He means: so what? Putting it in the כלי should change nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of the תנאים that step 28 said רב follows.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רבי יוסי בן יוסי בן יאסיין and רבי יהודה הנחתום that the כלי is the cutoff.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided dilemma: either the unfit קמיצה is a service, so it is invalid right away, or it is not a service, so the כלי adds nothing. Neither option explains why the כלי matters.

steps.title: רב נחמן: it is a service, but it is finished only in the כלי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן takes back his question. The unfit קמיצה is a service, but the service is only complete once the handful is put in a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן then said: Really it is a service, but its service is not finished until he puts it into a כלי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers his own question and explains the logic of those תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He finds a middle option between the two sides of his dilemma. The unfit קמיצה does count as a service, so it can ruin the מנחה. But the service is not complete until the handful goes into the כלי, so only then is the מנחה ruined and the handful can no longer be put back.

keyTerms.meaning: He then said, after changing his mind.
Really, actually. It introduces the true explanation.
Its service was completed.

steps.whatToRemember: According to these תנאים, קמיצה and putting it in a כלי together make one service. An unfit person's service ruins the מנחה only once the whole service is complete.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman then said:
Really it is a service,
but its service is not complete
until he puts it into a vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma raised in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Middle path: it is a service, but only complete with the כלי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The unfit קמיצה must be either a full service or not a service at all, so the כלי cannot matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a service that is only completed once the handful goes into the כלי. So the מנחה is ruined only from that point.

steps.title: A new challenge begins: what if he did not sanctify it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a question on רב נחמן's answer: if so, even when he did not sanctify it… (the question continues on the next amud).
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even if he did not sanctify it,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new question against רב נחמן's answer. The question is only beginning here and finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said the service is completed by putting the handful in a כלי. The גמרא now points to the case where the handful was not yet sanctified, to test whether this answer really holds. The rest of the challenge comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. It takes the last answer and draws a problem from it.

phrases.english: If so,
even if he did not sanctify it,
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished here. The question continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ לֹא קִידֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge against רב נחמן's answer in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's explanation that the service is completed by putting the handful in a כלי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It draws a conclusion from רב נחמן's answer about the case where the handful was not sanctified. The full attack continues on the next amud.
